items.title: Composite double regularization
items.statement: Let $X,Y,Z$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over one scalar field, let $F:X\to Y$ and $G:Y\to Z$ be compact linear maps, and set $A:=G\circ F:X\to Z$. For spectral regularization families $R^G_\alpha:Z\to Y$ for $G^\dagger$ and $R^F_\gamma:Y\to X$ for $F^\dagger$, and a parameter rule $(\alpha,\gamma):(0,\infty)\times Z\to(0,\infty)^2$, define $T_\delta(z^\delta):=R^F_{\gamma(\delta,z^\delta)}(R^G_{\alpha(\delta,z^\delta)}z^\delta)$ for $z^\delta\in Z$. The order is fixed by the factorization: first regularize $G$, then $F$; no general identity $A^\dagger=F^\dagger G^\dagger$ is part of this definition.

references.title: Christina Brandt and Patrick Horn, Regularisation and Parameter Choice Rules for Composite Linear Inverse Problems, §2.1 and Theorem 1
references.locator: §2.1, equation (2), and Theorem 1 with its complete proof, printed pp. 2–3; the abstract/body order discrepancy is recorded in batch-6 notes.

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, full lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 5, §5.1, printed pp. 44–50; spectral filter reconstruction maps and their domains.

title: Factorized and composite linear inversion — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Commuting diagonal factors with an explicit composite estimator
items.statement: Let $X=Y=Z=\mathbb R^2$ with the Euclidean inner product, $F=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$, $G=\operatorname{diag}(3,4)$, and $A=G\circ F$. For $\alpha,\gamma>0$, use the Tikhonov maps $R^G_\alpha=(G^*G+\alpha I)^{-1}G^*$ and $R^F_\gamma=(F^*F+\gamma I)^{-1}F^*$. Compute the two-stage estimate $R^F_\gamma R^G_\alpha z$ for arbitrary $z=(z_1,z_2)$ and its limit as $\alpha,\gamma\downarrow0$.

references.title: Christina Brandt and Patrick Horn, Regularisation and Parameter Choice Rules for Composite Linear Inverse Problems, §2.1
Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 6

items.title: Rank-deficient noncommuting factors break pseudoinverse composition
items.statement: For every pair of bounded linear maps $F:X\to Y$ and $G:Y\to Z$ between real or complex Hilbert spaces, the Moore–Penrose inverse of their composite satisfies $(G\circ F)^\dagger=F^\dagger G^\dagger$.

references.title: Christina Brandt and Patrick Horn, Regularisation and Parameter Choice Rules for Composite Linear Inverse Problems, §2.1
Roger Penrose, A generalized inverse for matrices
